title: Spectral Graph Sparsification Preserves Representation Geometry in Graph Neural Networks
claim: Downstream representation error grows smoothly and roughly linearly with sparsification distortion, and this holds across different graph families.
layout: 3 panels in a row, shared x-axis, dashed linear fits with error bars
description: Three side-by-side scatter plots share the same x-axis, empirical sparsification distortion epsilon_emp, running from roughly 0.37 to 0.75. From left to right the panels are titled Relative Filter Error, Relative Representation and Relative Gram. Each panel plots two series with one-standard-deviation error bars. Blue points are the SBM graphs and green points are the geometric graphs. An orange dashed line fits the SBM points and a red dashed line fits the geometric points. The legend in the first panel gives the fitted slopes, 0.20 for SBM and 0.16 for geometric. The y-axes carry the matrix-norm error formulas. Every panel shows a monotonic, near-linear rise. In the second and third panels the SBM series sits well above the geometric series, which stays low and flat. The eye goes first to the diverging blue and green point clouds.
caption: Controlled validation of representation stability. We measure relative polynomial-filter error, relative hidden-representation error, and relative hidden-Gram error for effective resistance sparsified weighted SBM and geometric weighted k-NN graphs. The graph operator is the scaled combinatorial Laplacian ¯L = L/∥L∥2, and the polynomial filter is p(¯L) = I −0.6¯L + 0.15¯L2. Across both graph families, all three quantities increase smoothly with ϵemp, consistent with the stability predictions of Theorems 1–3. Markers show means over five sparsifier draws at each selected budget, and vertical error bars denote one standard deviation.
abstract: Spectral graph sparsification is a classical tool for reducing graph complexity while preserving Laplacian quadratic forms. In graph neural networks (GNNs), sparsification is often used to accelerate computation while maintaining predictive performance. In this work, we study a complementary representation-level question: does sparsification preserve the geometry of learned embeddings? For polynomial-filter GNNs, we prove that any $Îµ$-spectral sparsifier induces $O(Îµ)$ perturbations in polynomial graph filters, multilayer hidden representations, and their Gram matrices. These guarantees imply stability of squared pairwise distances, class means, and covariance structure in embedding space. We further establish finite-time training stability: under smoothness and boundedness assumptions, gradient descent on dense and sparsified graphs produces weight trajectories whose separation grows at most proportionally to the sparsification distortion. Empirically, effective-resistance sparsification validates the predicted perturbation chain on synthetic graphs and preserves hidden representation geometry on real datasets. In our experiments, the gram matrix and training dynamics show low divergence even under substantial sparsification, consistent with the predicted stability under spectral sparsification. Hidden Gram preservation strongly predicts neighborhood preservation and class-centroid stability across FashionMNIST, Cora, and Paul15. Together, these results show that spectral sparsification preserves not only graph operators, but also the representation geometry that supports downstream use of GNN embeddings for interpretability.
